quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Traffic signals sometimes show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same thing as a circular red traffic light.
It means drivers may turn in the direction the arrow points.
It means traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a circular red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow has the same meaning as a circular red traffic light. You must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: You are driving on a highway with two solid yellow lines dividing the lanes. What are you allowed to do?

options.text: Cross the lines only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
Cross the lines to pass other vehicles if there is no oncoming traffic.
Never cross the lines.
Cross the lines only to make a U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the lines only to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction. You may only cross them to turn left into an alley, private road, or driveway.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you increase your vehicle's speed?

options.text: It increases.
It decreases.
It makes cross traffic easier to see.
It has no effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: It decreases.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the smaller your field of vision becomes. As your speed increases, you must be extra alert to potential hazards.

questions.question: A vehicle coming toward you is using high beams. Where should you look?

options.text: Either side of the road
The center of the road
The right side of the road
The left side of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The right side of the road
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the other vehicle's headlights and helps you stay on course until the vehicle passes.

questions.question: From the center lane, what can you do?

options.text: You may make left turns.
You may make U-turns.
You may pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns.
questions.explanation: The center lane is only for left-turning vehicles from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or for driving straight through.

questions.question: What do regulatory signs do?

options.text: They are placed everywhere there is danger.
They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
They are diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
They warn drivers about school zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: They tell drivers what they must or must not do.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually rectangular with black markings on a white background. They tell drivers what they must or must not do. They show speed limits, no passing zones, no turning rules, and other driving regulations.

questions.question: You stop completely at an intersection, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe. This matches which traffic light?

options.text: A solid red light
A flashing yellow light
A solid green light
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: On a multilane road with traffic going in opposite directions, how should you use the shared center lane?

options.text: To pass other vehicles
To slow down or stop before turning left
As a through-traffic lane when traffic is slow
As a parking lane

questions.correctAnswerText: To slow down or stop before turning left
questions.explanation: Only enter the center lane when you have time to slow down or stop for a safe left turn. Never use it for passing or driving straight through.

questions.question: Why is it important to be alert to motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
They rarely use headlights.
Motorcyclists are less skilled drivers.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can easily hide in your blind spot. It is difficult to judge distance and speed with motorcycles, so always be extra cautious around them.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
Force the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the main road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles traveling in the opposite direction at least half of the main road. Both vehicles need adequate space to pass each other safely.

questions.question: A red and white triangular sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is coming.
Look both ways before crossing.
Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular yield sign means you must slow down and give the right-of-way to other vehicles or pedestrians. Be ready to stop if you need to.

questions.question: Drivers should look ahead ____ seconds down the road.

options.text: 10 seconds
12 seconds
5 seconds
3 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 seconds
questions.explanation: Always look 12 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops or dangerous turns.

questions.question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you on a one-way street, you must:

options.text: Turn on your hazard lights.
Move to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights approaches on a one-way street, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Leave extra space when stopping:

options.text: On a hill.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll booth.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on a hill. If the car in front rolls backward when traffic moves, extra space reduces the chance of a crash.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Stay right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: If traffic lights are not working:

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers your plans.
Turn on your hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Take turns with other drivers and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly in:

options.text: Flat areas.
Curvy areas.
Sunny areas.
Shaded areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded areas.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, roads freeze faster in shaded areas under trees or buildings. These areas also take longer to dry.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Any lights work the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: To turn left on a multilane, one-way street, start from:

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Start left turns from the left lane on multilane streets.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after alcohol:

options.text: Lowers blood alcohol level.
Removes the effects of alcohol.
Does not change blood alcohol level.
Raises blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol level. While it may keep you awake, it cannot change how much alcohol is in your blood or make you sober.

questions.question: Hydroplaning is usually caused by:

options.text: Excessive stops.
Sudden stops.
Sudden turns.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: As you drive faster, your tires cannot clear water from the road as well. If you drive too fast, your tires may lose grip and your vehicle will slide on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: A bicyclist who does not obey traffic laws:

options.text: Is allowed to break traffic laws because bicyclists do not have to follow them.
Can be ticketed.
Will always receive a warning from law enforcement.
Will have their bicycle taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be ticketed.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. Bicyclists who do not obey traffic laws can receive a ticket.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to cross after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
After one train passes, check the other track for a second train before crossing.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check the other track for a second train before crossing.
questions.explanation: With two railroad tracks next to each other, a second train may be on the other track. After one train passes, look both ways before crossing to make sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down before the curve, then speed up as you leave it.
Keep the same speed throughout the curve.
Speed up before the curve, then slow down as you leave it.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before the curve, then speed up as you leave it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you enter a curve and gradually speed up as you exit it. Speeding up when entering a curve makes it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that a ____ light will soon appear.

options.text: Flashing yellow
Steady green
Steady red
Flashing red

questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: An approaching driver does not dim their high beam headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get around them.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and cut in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as you can. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly can cause them to lose balance.

questions.question: You may cross double solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass a slow-moving truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into a driveway or to enter or exit a highway (where permitted).

questions.question: When approaching a work zone with a "45 mph where workers present" sign, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down right away.
Drive at a safe speed, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less when workers are present.
Merge to the right lane.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a safe speed, watch for workers, and slow to 45 mph or less when workers are present.
questions.explanation: In a work zone with a speed limit for when workers are present, you can drive at the regular speed when no workers are there. You must slow down to 45 mph or less when you see workers.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because the driver must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The maximum speed limit.
A speed that is faster than is reasonable and safe.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and safe. Adjust your speed based on the road, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting. Always stay within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: A solid white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: A community group is picking up trash ahead.
Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
Children are playing ahead.
A pedestrian crosswalk is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Workers are on or near the road in the work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that workers may be on or near the road ahead. Drive with extra care through this area.

questions.question: When an intersection is blocked by other traffic, you should:

options.text: Move slowly until traffic ahead clears.
Get as close as possible to the car in front of you.
Wait until you can drive completely through before entering.
Use your horn to make cars move forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can drive completely through before entering.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if you cannot drive all the way through. Wait for traffic ahead to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on an expressway. Move to the left lane when:

options.text: Traffic is heavy but moving steadily.
The weather is bad and roads are slippery.
Traffic is slow in your lane and cars are in the left lane.
Traffic is light and cars are merging onto the expressway from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is light and cars are merging onto the expressway from the right.
questions.explanation: Watch for merging vehicles on expressways. Move to another lane or adjust your speed to help merging drivers enter safely.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: One-way road.
No right turn.
Exit.
Sharp right turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp right turn ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a sharp right turn is coming up ahead.

questions.question: The correct way to use a freeway exit ramp is to:

options.text: Slow down before entering the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same while on the exit ramp.
Pass slower traffic on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp. Then slow down to match the exit speed.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes move in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes move in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: Unless posted otherwise, the minimum speed on freeways is:

options.text: 45 mph.
55 mph.
70 mph.
85 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The minimum freeway speed is 55 mph unless a different limit is posted. Follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a sign?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
An action is not allowed.
Some drivers must yield to others.
You must drive below the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means an action is forbidden. This sign is rectangular, white, with red and black markings. The red circle and slash over a symbol shows that action is not permitted.

questions.question: What is the best way to keep yourself and others safe when backing up?

options.text: Honk your horn before shifting into reverse.
Walk behind your vehicle to check before getting in the driver's seat.
Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
Turn up the radio before backing up to alert people around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk behind your vehicle to check before getting in the driver's seat.
questions.explanation: Backing up is risky because drivers cannot see well behind their vehicles. Before getting in the driver's seat, walk to the back of the vehicle to check for children and small objects.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn.
A road joins from the right.
The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
Winding road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Guide signs are ____ signs that show direction and distance information.

options.text: Yellow
Red
Green
White

questions.correctAnswerText: Green
questions.explanation: Guide signs have a green background and show direction and distance to places. They help drivers find their way in unfamiliar areas.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights makes your pupils contract. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What does this sign show?

options.text: Right turn.
Intersection.
Lane change.
Road curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gas?

options.text: Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.
Speeding up quickly.
Slowing down gradually.
Braking suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every sudden stop uses fuel to speed up again. Drivers who look ahead can slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid hard braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic going the same direction.
During daylight only.
At any time.
When making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making a turn.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You can only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the road slants toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: An intersection is coming up.
You are near a construction area.
You will be required to turn left soon.
The road will get narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will get narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge marks the boundary between the driving lane and shoulder. If the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What should drivers do when a vehicle with Anti-Lock Brakes loses traction on a slippery road?

options.text: Pump the brakes.
Press and hold the brake pedal down.
Press and hold the gas pedal.
Lightly tap the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: If you lose traction, press hard on the brake pedal, hold it steady, and steer to safety. The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will pump the brakes automatically. If you stop pressing or pump the brakes yourself, you will turn off the ABS.
